findings.text: follow-on: `_require_configured_override_path` refuses `backends.<name>`/`roles.<name>` for a name no layer defines, and this refusal lives only on the dry-run branch (reckon/cli.py:1655) — the non-dry dispatch path still merges an unknown keyed-map name. A caller who defines a backend entirely through repeated --set (e.g. `--set backends.ephemeral.launch=cli --set backends.ephemeral.command=... `) gets a dry-run refusal but a real dispatch that merges the section, so the preview and the launch disagree about what is valid on the very plan (`a-dry-run-must-resolve-what-the-real-call-resolves`) this node implements. The node flags this in follow_ons ("Only the dry run refuses it, per section s6's dry-run scope"), so it is a declared, scoped follow-on rather than an undisclosed defect; a phantom name is harmless (it merges into a section nothing routes to), which is why the impact is parity-of-message rather than a spent run.

follow-on: `override_resolution` is returned but only attached to the success payload (reckon/cli.py:1805, guarded by `if override_resolution`). The contract-validation branch (exit 2) and the lane-paused branch (exit 75) between the call at 1655 and the emit at 1806 both raise before the payload is built, so their refusal documents carry no override echo. This is consistent with section s6's done-when, which scopes the echo to the dry-run output rather than to every dry-run exit, and no test covers those branches; note it because a caller keying on a `dry_run:true` refusal cannot tell an override that failed to resolve from one that resolved against a held lane.

follow-on: probed independently at head — `--set fences.ghost_key=1` and `--set backends.codex.ghost_sub=1` both exit 1 with a plain `Error: <override>: <path>: Extra inputs are not permitted` line (schema validation, no JSON document), whereas `--set backends.ghost.budget_group=null` exits 1 with the new JSON refusal. The done-when ("A path the configuration does not know is refused naming it") is met by both, and the schema refusal names the path and predates this node, so this is not a regression; but one dry-run refusal is parseable and its sibling is not, so a caller that decodes JSON to read the refusal silently receives nothing for the leaf-key case.
